packs.title: Craters, Collections & Harbour
packs.promise: Meet Auckland through art, museum evidence, an ancestral mountain and a harbour crossing to Devonport.

q.s: Take a colour question from a gallery work into an original city scene.
st: Before entering the galleries, leave umbrellas, backpacks, shopping bags and large bags in the free cloakroom; bags must stay off your back in the galleries. Visitors under 14 must be accompanied by an adult. Enter an open free general-collection exhibition around 12:45. Choose one work with a readable artist/title label and two colours you can describe.
Write how those colours relate: close together, widely separated, strong against quiet, or another observed relationship. Keep interpretation separate from the label.

Make an original scene of an Auckland afternoon using that colour relationship. A short description can replace drawing; do not copy the work’s composition, distinctive motifs or culturally restricted imagery.
Name the work and artist that prompted your colour question, then give your own scene a title.

q.s: Pause where a garden’s glass structure meets the Domain.
st: Choose an open public path position outside the Wintergarden glasshouses, or a comfortable public courtyard position if it is open. Do not wait at a locked gate.
For two minutes, follow a line of the glass structure and then a line made by nearby planting. Let your eyes settle on one detail of each.
Write how their edges differ, using ordinary descriptions rather than guessing a plant’s name or a building’s age.
Take a few unhurried breaths and record which detail you want to remember when you enter the museum.

q.t: A Small Exhibition with a Question
q.s: Make a miniature exhibition from two labelled museum objects.
st: Obtain applicable general admission around 12:30–12:45: international adult NZ$32; Auckland residents free with proof; other New Zealand residents by donation. Special exhibitions/experiences are separate. Before entering galleries, follow the Museum’s bag rules: Services excludes large bags, backpacks and tripods; Conditions specifically requires tripods and bags over 40 cm long, 15 cm wide and 35 cm high to be checked into a self-service locker. Charges apply; check current storage arrangements. Children aged 13 and under must be with an adult at all times inside the Museum. Find an open natural-history gallery using the map or a host’s directions. Allow ticket, locker and works-related entrance time in addition to the 100 minutes inside, finish well before 17:00, and follow current public visitor entrance signs.
Choose two displayed objects or specimens with readable labels. Record the name and one stated place, material, period or use for each; leave missing information unknown.
Invent a title for a two-object exhibition that links a question these objects raise. Write a short caption for each, keeping observed details and label facts distinguishable.
Add one question your tiny exhibition cannot answer. Do not invent an object’s origin or turn a taonga’s cultural meaning into decorative imagery.

packs.title: Downtown Waterfront
packs.promise: Follow Auckland’s public waterfront through arrival spaces, a maritime collection and the shapes of Wynyard Quarter.

q.s: Collect the parts of Te Rou Kai before reading their connection to this shore.
st: Find Te Rou Kai in Takutai Square. From the dry public paving, choose one sculptural stone, a second differently shaped stone and a piece of the surrounding square.
Record three contrasts in outline, surface or spacing. Do not touch, climb or count on the fountain running.
Read any open interpretation, or the linked Britomart description, about the artwork’s connection to the former foreshore and kaimoana. Keep that source evidence separate from your observations.
Choose which of your three details you would use to orient someone arriving at the square. Explain where to stand to find it.

q.s: Make a small drawing from the meeting of city paving and harbour water.
st: Choose a safe public position where you can see the shape of the waterfront platform, a planted area and the harbour beyond.
Find a straight line made by the city and a curved line near the water. Trace their relationship in a tiny sketch, or describe it in two sentences.
Make an original three-colour scene using those lines. Colours can be named in words; do not copy an artwork’s cultural motifs or interpret an ecological feature from appearance alone.
Give the scene a title that refers to the meeting of land and water.

q.s: Turn a museum boat detail into a design question of your own.
st: Obtain the applicable museum admission and use the visitor map to find an open vessel or vessel-model display. Aim for entry by 14:30 and allow 75 minutes inside, before 17:00 closing. If you have a backpack or large bag, deposit it at the complimentary ticket-desk bag check before entering the galleries. All minors must be accompanied by a supervising adult at all times.
Read its label for one stated purpose, journey or use. Observe a feature of its shape or construction, keeping your own guess separate from the label.
Design a small imaginary vessel for one everyday cargo, such as a bag of books. Explain one shape choice and one question you would ask a real boatbuilder.
Name the museum display that prompted the question, then mark your design as your own. Do not copy a culturally distinctive vessel design or claim it would be seaworthy.
